title: The Data Center Backlash Bursts Into the Midterms
partialText: With opposition to the centers mounting, many Democrats and a growing number of Republicans are campaigning against them.

title: Jeffries and Kushner Meet Privately as Midterm Attacks Fly
partialText: President Trump’s son-in-law and the man in line to be speaker of a Democratic-led House discussed how Democrats and the administration could work together.

title: Angry Ohio Voters Could Turn Their State Purple Again
partialText: A governor’s race, a Senate contest and enough congressional contests to swing control of the House are all in play in Ohio, where voters of all stripes express a deep sense of powerlessness.

title: The Midterms Feel Like 2006 All Over Again
partialText: With an unpopular war and high prices agitating voters, members of both parties see parallels to an election cycle when Democrats romped. But a lot has changed.

title: What Canadian Goods Will Take Trump’s 50% Tariffs? Some Pretty Strange Items.
partialText: Buoys, dog muzzles, capes, national flags and “base metal statuettes” from Canada are now more expensive for U.S. shoppers.

title: U.S.-Canada Trade War: What to Know About Tariffs and the Negotiations
partialText: Canada suspended trade negotiations, triggering President Trump’s 50 percent tariffs on a range of Canadian goods. Mark Carney said he would retaliate “dollar for dollar.”

title: The U.S. Start-Up Making Low-Cost Interceptors for the Iran War
partialText: For Florida-based Powerus, becoming a global supplier of counterdrone technology has meant involving the Trumps, a golf course and a new way of doing business.

title: Iran Warns Gulf States Not to Join Trump’s Economic War
partialText: Iran’s new hard-line national security adviser, Mohsen Rezaei, vowed to prevent “a single drop of oil” from leaving the region.

title: America’s Desert Metropolis Is on the Short List to Lose Water
partialText: Decades ago, Arizona won funding for a massive Colorado River project by agreeing to be first in line for cuts at a time of deep drought. The Trump administration says that time has come.

title: Wildfires Are Turning Forests in the American West Into Shrubland
partialText: Towering woodlands in the West are being permanently replaced by tracts of spiky shrubs. Conditions “just aren’t normal anymore,” one researcher said.

title: How Big Tech Captured American Schools
partialText: Companies like Google and Microsoft have used their money, their might and their massive reach to influence nearly every step of the education supply chain.

title: Someone Was Impersonating Collien Fernandes Online. She Says It Was Her Husband.
partialText: The German actress Collien Fernandes set out to discover who was pretending to be her online and sending men sexually explicit material. Her answer ignited a feminist movement.

title: Twitter Broke the Left. X Will Break the Right.
partialText: Democrats paid a price for forming their politics on Twitter; the right will pay a price for forming theirs on X.

title: The Barbie Backlash
partialText: ‘The Odyssey’ and ‘Barbie’ show a zeitgeist shift that goes beyond Hollywood: The hero’s narrative is corroding our political and public life.

title: A Murder Trial in Massachusetts
partialText: How the trial of Lindsay Clancy has become a proxy for how people view society’s ills.

title: Echoing Trump, Latin America’s Leaders Boost Allies Across Borders
partialText: With cheers, endorsements and insults for rivals and “wokismo,” a new crop of right-wing leaders are openly stepping into one another’s elections.
